title: The sealed trial identity does not commit to the required artifact and provenance closure
claim: A trial can seal with an empty pre-effect artifact reservation and without the expected output, resolved experiment, integrity record, trajectory, or complete retained-file closure; verification accepts added files and a corrupted durable intent.

evidence.detail: run_trial publishes IntentRecord.artifacts as an empty vector while naming an expected-output key that is never staged.
Agent and verifier artifact read failures are ignored with if-let-Ok, so promised evidence can disappear before sealing.
The trajectory is projected in memory but only a pre_seal_digest is copied to the unsealed receipt; no trajectory or resolved experiment/integrity record is inserted into the bundle.
RunBundle::verify hashes only manifest.body.entries and never checks unreferenced files, intent.json, settlement.json, expected_output, or intent artifact equality.
After adding artifacts/native/rogue.txt, regrade returned outcome=verified and exit 0; after replacing intent.json with non-JSON bytes, regrade again returned verified and exit 0.

reproduction: Run the hermetic phase18-local experiment, add bundle/artifacts/native/rogue.txt, then run opi-eval regrade --root <run-root>.
Replace a sealed bundle's intent.json with invalid bytes, then run opi-eval regrade --root <run-root>.

title: Offline reporting trusts mutable side files and publishes after bundle verification fails
claim: Report recomputation reads run-report.json and receipt.json outside the sealed bundle, derives headline and coverage values from them, and unconditionally publishes with exit 0 even when RunBundle::verify reports mutation; its --out path can also overwrite a sealed or prior artifact.

evidence.detail: recompute_from_bundle loads mutable run-report.json for declared trials, identities, denominator, and coverage.
Bundle verification failure is reduced to a mutation-detected display token; it does not stop report construction.
Per-trial receipt.json is read separately from the sealed manifest.
render always emits outcome=published, including when bundle_verification contains Failed.
headline takes the reward from mutable receipt.verifier and uses the manifest only for an artifact digest label.
The unrestricted --out destination is written directly and report_exit_code returns 0 for every published report.
artifact_path creates parent directories even when called by read-only verification, so a damaged sealed tree can be mutated by regrade/report.
After overwriting a covered agent-answer artifact, report printed state=mutation-detected but outcome=published and exited 0.

reproduction: Overwrite one manifest-covered artifact, then run opi-eval report --root <run-root>; observe mutation-detected together with outcome=published and exit 0.
Run opi-eval report --root <run-root> --out <run-root>/trials/<trial>/bundle/manifest.json; the CLI overwrites the sealed manifest.

title: Agent-owned failures are reclassified as infrastructure and bypass native grading
claim: For valid tasks, any AgentCompletion::Failed stops GradeDispatch and the resulting TrialFact is InfrastructureFailure, contrary to the registered rule that Agent crashes and Agent-owned timeouts remain Agent outcomes scored under the native grader.

evidence.detail: Every AgentCompletion::Failed records its boundary on the authority ledger before grade dispatch.
GradeDispatch is refused for agent-process, adapter, evidence, and infrastructure boundaries.
Every failed Agent is mapped to TrialOutcome::InfrastructureFailure.
The acceptance test explicitly asserts zero verifier executions for agent timeout/missing evidence.
The timeout/cancellation test expects infrastructure-failure comparability, so the passing suite asserts the opposite of P18-FAL-003.

title: Natural child exit can leave descendants alive while cleanup is reported as not required
claim: When the direct child exits normally, the supervisor does not terminate or verify its process tree; descendants that keep inherited pipes open are abandoned after EOF grace while cleanup is recorded as NotRequired.

evidence.detail: The natural ExitState::Exited branch settles readers and returns CleanupEvidence::NotRequired without calling TreeGuard::terminate or verify_terminated.
settle_reader silently abandons a drain when a descendant still holds the pipe and records no cleanup uncertainty.
Unix tree termination exists but is invoked only by the timeout/cancellation branch; unlike the Windows JobGuard, the Unix guard has no Drop cleanup.
Current tests cover a natural-exit/cancel race and timeout descendants, but not a direct child that exits 0 after starting a surviving background descendant.

reproduction: Supervise a shell that starts a background sleep inheriting stdout and exits 0; after EOF_GRACE, observe cleanup=not-required while the descendant process remains alive.

title: DeepSWE accepts out-of-domain rewards and treats any structurally verified oracle result as passing
claim: The Pier importer accepts any finite integer reward, casts negative values to u64 (turning -1 into 0) and accepts values above the native range; the DeepSWE oracle preflight then accepts every Verified completion without checking its reward.

evidence.detail: import_pier_job_result validates only finiteness and an integer fraction, not the native reward domain.
reward as u64 silently maps negative floating-point values to zero and retains values greater than one.
run_oracle_preflight hard-codes deepswe-v1.1 => true for every BenchmarkCompletion::Verified.
Existing importer tests cover a positive Harbor aggregate and trial-count drift, but no negative, greater-than-one, or zero DeepSWE oracle result.

reproduction: Feed import_pier_job_result a one-trial result.json whose reward key is -1; observe Fact::Known value 0 instead of a parse failure.
Run the DeepSWE oracle preflight with a structurally valid native result whose reward is zero; observe that the preflight is accepted.

title: Every durable trial intent is bound to the first comparison edge
claim: The N-subject schema and comparison assembler support multiple directed edges, but run_trial assigns every trial bundle's PairIdentity from experiment.edges().first(), so later edges cannot retain their own durable pair identity.

evidence.detail: PairIdentity is always constructed from experiment.edges().first() for every declared trial.
ComparisonSet iterates the full edge set, leaving the report-level shape inconsistent with the durable bundle intent.
The N-subject test stops at resolution; no test executes a multi-edge experiment and inspects bundle intent identities.
P18-A20 resolves the generic fixture but does not exercise run_trial, sealing, regrade, or report.

reproduction: Execute a valid multi-edge experiment and inspect trials/*/bundle/intent.json; every intent.pair equals the first declared edge rather than the edge owning that trial pair.
